title: Descriptors and class creation hooks
masterChecklist: Descriptors, decorators, metaclasses, class creation hooks — advanced/internals
Dunder methods: representation, comparison, arithmetic, container, context-manager, iterator protocols
Framework design trade-offs, explicitness, introspection and maintainable abstractions
whyItMatters: Some Python features that look simple—properties, ORM fields, validation frameworks—are built on deeper hooks. Understanding them helps you read advanced libraries and avoid inventing unnecessary magic.
simpleExplanation: A descriptor is an object assigned to a class attribute that controls attribute access through methods such as __get__ and __set__. A class creation hook can validate or register subclasses when they are defined. These tools are powerful, so they should be used only when a simpler function, property, or composition would not express the design clearly.
mentalModel: A descriptor is a trained receptionist at a class doorway: every read or write passes through a consistent policy. A class creation hook is an orientation checklist applied when a new kind of employee is added to the organization.
outcomes: Use __init_subclass__ for a simple subclass registration policy.
State why advanced class magic should be kept small and documented.

realWorldExample.scenario: A learning platform has several model classes that each need a validated title field.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: Copying the same setter into every class leads to inconsistent rules; a custom metaclass can hide behavior so thoroughly that maintainers cannot debug it.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Use a small descriptor only when the shared rule is truly common, document its behavior, and prefer an ordinary property for one-class validation.

explanation: __set_name__ learns the public attribute name when the Lesson class is created.
__get__ returns the stored value for an instance and returns the descriptor itself for class-level access.
The descriptor centralizes one validation rule, but it is more complex than a single property.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Try Lesson('') and explain which descriptor method enforces the rule.

procedure: First ask whether a normal function, dataclass, or property is clearer.
If a rule must be shared across many classes, define its public behavior and error messages.
Keep descriptor storage names private by convention and test class/instance access.
Use class creation hooks only for explicit registration or validation rules.
Document hidden behavior so a reader can understand attribute access without guessing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a metaclass for a problem solved by a decorator or __init_subclass__.
commonMistakes.why: Metaclasses affect class creation broadly and are difficult to debug.
commonMistakes.avoid: Choose the least powerful abstraction that expresses the rule.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting instance is None in descriptor __get__.
commonMistakes.why: Class-level introspection can then behave unexpectedly.
commonMistakes.avoid: Define and test both class and instance access behavior.

commonMistakes.mistake: Hiding important validation in magic without documentation.
commonMistakes.why: Callers cannot understand why a normal assignment fails.
commonMistakes.avoid: Write a clear public contract and ordinary error message.

lab.title: Share a non-empty text rule with a descriptor
lab.safety: Uses only an in-memory fictional lesson title.
guidedSteps: Return self for class-level access in __get__.
Read the private stored name for an instance.
Create Lesson('  Loops  '), print its stripped title, then catch ValueError from Lesson('') and check Lesson.title is a NonEmptyText descriptor.
checks: Rejects blank titles and strips valid title text.
hints: if instance is None: return self
lab.solutionExplanation: The descriptor applies the same small rule every time the public attribute is assigned. The lab proves normalization, rejection and class-level access rather than only defining the descriptor.
challenges: Predict Lesson.title before any instance is created.
Find the bug: omit instance is None in __get__.
Experiment: create a second class that reuses NonEmptyText for its name field.

projectConnection.milestone: Choose between a property and a descriptor for shared validation, then document the reasoning in a short design note.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: The team can explain the descriptor's public behavior and why a simpler alternative was or was not sufficient.

assessment.question: What can a descriptor control?
assessment.answer: How an attribute is read, assigned, or deleted through descriptor methods.
assessment.explanation: It is a class-level mechanism behind several Python features.

assessment.question: When should you prefer a simple property?
assessment.answer: When validation belongs to one class and a property expresses it clearly.
assessment.explanation: Advanced abstraction is not automatically better.

assessment.question: Why check instance is None in __get__?
assessment.answer: To define sensible class-level access such as Lesson.title.
assessment.explanation: Class and instance access have different needs.
